_note: Full English translation of every story and tutorial text. Flat table key -> string; keys are identical to story_ru.json (a test checks it). %d / %s placeholders must stay.
fuel.title: Fuel station
fuel.s1: Hello, Gran? I've got a drill now. It eats fuel, and fuel means peat. The cellar's full of peat.
fuel.g1: And what, I'm supposed to carry it to you from Thailand by the bucket?
fuel.s2: No need. I want a station: I distil the peat, I refuel, I go down with a full tank.
fuel.g2: You'll get your station. One condition: the fertiliser from the still is mine — it's worth its weight in gold in Thailand. The blocks are yours.
fuel.n1: Three days later there was a hut in the garden with a tank and a hose. Robert had even painted it.
fuel.n2: The station hummed by the fence. It smelled of peat and something else.
fuel.s3: The fertiliser goes to her. Well, at least it's not interest.
fuel.toast: A fuel station went up in the garden. Peat goes into the still, fuel into the tank, fertiliser to Granny.
quest.gold: Task: dig the gold with Grandpa's pickaxe — %d left
quest.gold_done: Five nuggets in the backpack. Now the foundation.
quest.gold_first_toast: Gold first. Five nuggets on level four — they're highlighted.
quest.gold_needs_pickaxe: A shovel can't take gold. You need a pickaxe — Grandpa's is in the workshop, in the corner behind the mops.
quest.foundation_needs_pickaxe: The shovel hit the old foundation. Only a pickaxe will take it — it's in the workshop, in the corner behind the mops.
quest.garden_left_of_stairs: Nothing to dig here — start to the right of the stairs.
quest.foundation: Task: break through the foundation with the pickaxe
quest.sell: Task: sell the gold at the workshop
quest.food: Task: order food at the front door
intro_grandpa.title: Grandpa
intro_grandpa.card_when:
The summer before last.
Koldobino village.
intro_grandpa.n1: Grandpa was digging potatoes. Forty years of digging, and he'd never found anything more interesting in that soil. Until one day a little yellow stone glinted in his bucket.
intro_grandpa.g1: Come and have breakfast! It's getting cold!
intro_grandpa.s3: In a minute, in a minute. There's a vein here, I can feel it.
intro_grandpa.g2: Get out of there. Do you hear me? Get out!
intro_grandpa.s4: Just a little more — and I'll climb out.
intro_grandpa.g_call3: You'll bury yourself alive down there! Get out this minute!
intro_grandpa.s_call3: One more swing — and that's it, home.
intro_grandpa.card_death:
They found him on the fourth day.
Shovel beside him. Palm full of gold.
intro_grandpa.g3: You asked for it, you old fool. Lie right there. Next to your garden.
intro_grandpa.n7: Granny buried him in the yard. And sold the gold. Almost all of it.
intro_boy.title: Grandson
intro_boy.n1: The grandson did well at school. Then okay. Then however it went.
intro_boy.s1: What? Everything's on the internet anyway.
intro_boy.n2: His parents were upset at first. Then they shouted. Then they quietly bought a bus ticket.
intro_boy.p1: Summer at Gran's. No internet. You'll come back a human being.
intro_boy.s2: To the village?! There's nothing there!
intro_boy.n3: Behind a blank three-metre fence stood a house that had no business in this village. Double glazing. Air conditioning. A car under the canopy — and it cost more than the school.
intro_boy.g1: Come in, don't just stand there. Wash your hands and sit down.
intro_boy.s4: Gran. Where did all this come from?
intro_boy.g2: From your grandfather. He found gold in that garden. And buried himself right there, the old fool.
intro_boy.g3: Forget it. I picked it clean — there's nothing left.
intro_boy.n4: He didn't forget. He thought of nothing else until morning.
intro_boy.card_morning: In the morning Granny was flying off to Thailand.
intro_boy.g4: Three weeks. Stay out of the garden. The shovel's in the shed, but you haven't seen it.
intro_boy.n5: The gate clicked. The yard went very quiet.
intro_boy.card_shovel: The shovel was in the shed.
tutorial_dig.hint: Pull the joystick down — the hero digs beneath himself. Sideways he walks, and when he hits earth he starts digging.
autodig.title: By itself
autodig.card_start: After that he dug without thinking.
autodig.n_done: By dark there was no garden left — just a pit three cells deep. Grandpa had started with one just like it.
autodig.toast_done: The garden is dug out three cells deep. The stairs by the house — on the left — lead out of the pit.
dud_treasure.title: First find
dud_treasure.item_text: A tin candy box. Inside: a handful of coins and five green banknotes folded in four.
dud_treasure.n2: He kept the box anyway. A first find is a first find: those go in a museum, not into your pocket.
dud_treasure.card_collection:
The find went into the collection:
Antiquity branch, slot 1.
workshop.title: Workshop
workshop.n1: The shovel clanged against something that shouldn't be in the ground. Concrete. Flat, smooth, the full width of the garden.
workshop.s1: Some kind of slab. A foundation, maybe?
workshop.n2: You can't dig concrete with a shovel. You need a pickaxe. He didn't have one — but there was a cellar Granny had never said a word about.
workshop.n3: The cellar smelled of machine oil and old iron, and a bare bulb on a wire swung with every step.
workshop.n4: The workbench had stood untouched for two years. Under the dust: a blueprint, a jar of nuts and bolts, a dried-up mug of tea.
workshop.n5: He wiped the bench with his sleeve. Cleared a corner: mops, rakes, a bucket with no bottom, two fishing rods.
workshop.n6: And behind all of it — there it was.
workshop.item_text:
The handle is smooth, worn glossy by someone else's palms. The iron is rusty, but sharp.
You found a pickaxe. Now you can dig more than dirt — you can mine minerals: stone, gold and everything deeper.
workshop.toast_pickaxe: You have Grandpa's pickaxe! Now you can mine more than dirt — minerals: stone, gold and everything deeper.
death.title: Like Grandpa
death.n2: The wall was taller than he was. He jumped. His fingers slid down the earth.
death.n4: Nobody came. Granny was in Thailand, the fence was blank, and this house hadn't had neighbours since spring.
death.card_same: Grandpa died exactly the same way.
death.n5: He woke up at home in bed with a splitting headache. His backpack lay beside him — everything in place, not a pebble lost.
death.n6: That's not how it works. But it happened.
death.s3: I'm not going down again without a ladder.
death.card_bars:
Health. Hunger. Energy.
Look top left — you've got them now.
death.toast_bars: The hunger and energy bars drain all the time, and three times faster under the pickaxe. An empty bar eats into your health.
backpack.title: The crate
backpack.n1: From then on he never left the house without the backpack. And he did call Granny in the end. The conversation was short and loud.
backpack.n2: There was a crate under the workbench. Grandpa had padlocked it, and the key, it seemed, went with him.
backpack.s1: Two hits. That's all it'll take.
backpack.n3: The lock gave on the second hit.
backpack.item_text: Two screws, straps, a toggle on the side. Grandpa built it himself — and never put it on.
backpack.s2: Oh, Grandpa. If you'd worn it back then, you'd have flown out of that pit.
backpack.r1: I'm Robert. Your granny sent me. Don't dig the garden any more.
backpack.s3: Then how do I get down?
backpack.r2: I'll make a proper way in. Not a pit. Wait at home — I'll come and tell you.
backpack.n4: He listened — for the first time since the start of summer. And went home.
robert.title: Robert
robert.n1: Two days later someone knocked on the front door.
robert.r2: Two days. Filled in the garden. The only way down now is the tunnel.
robert.n2: He left through the same door he'd knocked on. For Robert, that had been a long speech.
robert.toast_tunnel: The garden is closed for good. The only way into the mine is Robert's tunnel.
sleep1.title: Sleep
sleep1.n1: His legs gave out somewhere in the middle of the yard.
sleep1.n2: He reached the bed on sheer willpower.
sleep1.card_rules:
Sleep restores energy: 12.5% per game hour.
You can't sleep less than two hours, and more than eight is pointless.
sleep1.s1: Eight hours. Out like a light.
sleep2.title: Energy bar
sleep2.n1: It was forty cells up to the house. He had strength for two.
sleep2.n2: Something rustled in the side pocket of his backpack. Granny. Of course, Granny.
sleep2.item_text: A crumpled bar in foil. The expiry date rubbed out with a thumb.
sleep2.card_rules:
A bar removes all fatigue and half your hunger.
They're on sale now — the shop has opened a stimulants section.
intro_grandpa.item_text: Heavy, warm, as if alive. So that little stone in the bucket was no accident.
intro_grandpa.item_text2: The second one today. His hand reaches for the shovel on its own.
intro_grandpa.item_text3: The third. Time to stop — but he keeps digging.
intro_grandpa.s_trapped: Okay... easy now... stay calm. I'll climb out in a moment.
intro_grandpa.n_trapped: Six cells down. The walls sheer, smooth — and taller than he was. He tried to climb out. He really did.
grave_call.n1: His phone buzzed in his pocket. Granny, calling from Thailand like she was in the next room.
grave_call.s1: Hello. Gran, I just came up, my hands are covered in dirt, talk fast.
grave_call.g1: Alive? Not bad. Listen, before the line drops.
grave_call.g2: There's a slab on Grandpa's grave. Under the slab is a tea tin, and in the tin is his notebook.
grave_call.s2: A notebook? You never mentioned it.
grave_call.g3: I never mentioned a lot of things. I buried it with him. A week later I dug it up — he couldn't rest without it.
grave_call.g4: Read it in order. He sealed the pages, so you can't skip ahead.
grave_call.n2: The line cut out. The grave was two steps away — by the garden fence, right of the door.
grave_call.toast: Visit Grandpa's grave — by the garden fence, right of the door.
grave_call.title: The call
diary_first.n1: The gravestone slid aside easily: someone had moved it before. Underneath stood a tea tin.
diary_first.n2: Inside lay a notebook in green oilcloth, held shut with a rubber band.
diary_first.item_text: The oilcloth is rubbed through. The pages are held by paper strips, each saying: "Do not open until you get there."
diary_first.s1: He sealed them, too. Grandpa, who were you even writing for?
diary_first.d1: For whoever digs after me. For a fool, in other words.
diary_first.n3: He must have imagined it. Of course he did. But the voice was his — stubborn, as if arguing in advance.
diary_first.d2: First page is open. The rest you earn. Don't get greedy.
diary_first.s3: "Don't get greedy." From the man who buried himself in a vegetable patch.
diary_first.n4: He opened the first page. The handwriting was angry and hurried, the letters climbing over each other.
diary_first.toast: Grandpa's diary stays by the grave. New pages open by themselves — as you go deeper and get things done.
diary_first.title: The diary
first_artifact.n1: This find wasn't coins and it wasn't a tin box. It was old. Truly old — older than people and fences.
first_artifact.s1: Gran always said: "That goes in a museum, not up for sale." I think I'm starting to see what she meant.
first_artifact.n2: He turned it over. It was warm, as if someone had just been holding it.
first_artifact.s2: This isn't a vegetable patch anymore. There's really something down here.
first_artifact.n3: So Grandpa wasn't digging for nothing. He just didn't know when to stop.
first_artifact.title: A real find
depth_100.n1: A hundred cells. Overhead — earth, a house and one stern fence.
depth_100.s1: Grandpa couldn't get out of a six-cell pit. And here I am at a hundred — still breathing.
depth_100.g1: Robert reported: "Deep." That's the whole report.
depth_100.g2: Don't get cocky. A hundred is still a vegetable patch, just a long one.
depth_100.s3: Gran, I'm filing that under "well done".
depth_100.title: A hundred
fever_500.n1: Five hundred cells. Gold came thick, in veins, each one flaring in the lantern light.
fever_500.n2: He couldn't remember when he last ate. Couldn't tell whether it was day or night. Only the flashes.
fever_500.s1: Just a little more. There's a vein here, I can feel it.
fever_500.n3: He froze with the pickaxe in his hands. He'd heard that sentence before. Word for word.
fever_500.s2: ...That's what Grandpa used to say. Gran told me. Right before...
fever_500.n4: His arm kept reaching for another swing. He put the pickaxe on the ground — slowly, the way you set down something fragile.
fever_500.n5: In the side pocket he found a sandwich — Granny's, with dried-out cheese. He ate it and remembered he could, in fact, sleep.
fever_500.g2: Liar. But I like that you're ashamed.
fever_500.title: Fever
grandma_returns.n1: The gate creaked by the fence. Granny was back from Thailand — a day earlier than promised, tanned the colour of tea.
grandma_returns.g1: What are you staring at? A tan's a tan. Well, show me your marvel.
grandma_returns.s1: It's not a marvel, it's a drill-mobile. Digs sideways and down, and flies too.
grandma_returns.g2: Your grandfather drew things like that for years. I threw it all away except one sheet.
grandma_returns.g3: The very one. I put it there, on top. I knew you'd go poking around.
grandma_returns.s3: You said stay out of the garden.
grandma_returns.g4: I said stay out of the garden. I never said anything about the cellar.
grandma_returns.n2: She rummaged in her bag and took out something wrapped in a headscarf. Unwrapped it.
grandma_returns.item_text: The size of a pea. Grandpa brought it home in a bucket of potatoes, before the fever. The only gold Granny never sold.
grandma_returns.g5: It was a gift. The rest was the fever, and I don't keep fevers.
grandma_returns.g6: I didn't close the garden to keep you out. I closed it to keep the gold out. It turns anyone's head.
grandma_returns.s4: I noticed. Five hundred cells ago.
grandma_returns.g7: Then you're smarter than your grandfather. It's a low bar, mind.
grandma_returns.n3: She didn't fly back to Thailand. Said Thailand could wait, but her grandson couldn't.
grandma_returns.toast: Granny's back. Fewer secrets, no fewer nitpicks.
grandma_returns.title: Granny's back
whisper_1200.n1: Twelve hundred cells. It's quiet here. Too quiet: even the earth has stopped crumbling.
whisper_1200.v2: A little more. The yellowest is down there.
whisper_1200.n2: No answer. Only a tremor in the wall — polite, like a knock at the door.
whisper_1200.s3: I dig because I decided to. Do you hear me? Me.
whisper_1200.n3: He said it out loud — just in case, so both sides could hear.
whisper_1200.title: The voice
abyss_warning.n1: Thirty-nine hundred. The wall shuddered. Not a cave-in — cave-ins don't breathe.
abyss_warning.g1: I can hear something growling on your end. Is that your stomach?
abyss_warning.g2: Then listen and don't interrupt. Digging deeper without armour is stupidity.
abyss_warning.g3: The things in the museum aren't for display, they're clothing. Helmet, breastplate, shield, amulet, gauntlet. Collect all five.
abyss_warning.g4: I was married for fifty years to a stubborn man. I know more about holes in the ground than he did.
abyss_warning.n2: Digging alone wasn't enough anymore. Now he had to be able to hit back.
abyss_warning.toast: Below 4000 you dig with company. Gather a five-piece armour set from the museum.
abyss_warning.title: Breathing
bottom_near.n1: Ninety-seven hundred. Silence — as if someone were holding their breath along with him.
bottom_near.s1: Grandpa. I'm almost there. Can you hear me down there?
bottom_near.s2: I know. This is my last time down here.
bottom_near.n2: He checked the straps, the backpack and Granny's sandwich — in case he got hungry after the win.
bottom_near.toast: The bottom is close. It doesn't like guests.
bottom_near.title: Silence
ending.n1: Ten thousand cells. Everything fell silent. Completely.
ending.n2: It stopped mid-word. For the first time in years — or maybe ever.
ending.s1: So that's the whole voice. The whole fever.
ending.n3: Behind him, in the wall, lay the gold. Enough to fill in the garden. Twice. Three times.
ending.s2: A lot... You know, Grandpa, I don't need it.
ending.n4: He didn't take a single grain. The gold had killed Grandpa. It wasn't getting the grandson.
ending.s3: Let's go up. There's nothing more to listen to down here.
ending.n5: He climbed out by evening. The lights were on in the yard, and by the gate stood Granny, pretending she'd just come out to water the flowers.
ending.g1: You got out. Well, well. Your grandfather couldn't.
ending.g2: I see that. Dust yourself off.
ending.item_text: The first nugget. It doesn't belong to Granny any more.
ending.g3: It's yours. Put it on Grandpa's grave. Let him know how it ended.
ending.n6: He put the nugget on the gravestone and stood there a while.
ending.s5: I wish you hadn't dug, Grandpa. But thanks for digging.
ending.g4: Enough of the waterworks. Time to dig potatoes. Real ones.
ending.card2: The failing student went back to school. Didn't do any better. But he aced every problem about depth.
ending.card3: Granny lives in a house with a blank fence. The garden is under potatoes. Real ones.
ending.card4: Grandpa's pickaxe hangs over the workbench. Sometimes someone takes it. They always bring it back.
ending.toast: Ending reached. The game goes on — keep digging, just climb out in time.
ending.title: Enough
credits.c2:
Starring:
Grandpa — stubborn.
Granny — dry.
Grandson — grew up.
Robert — said nothing.
Potatoes — plenty.
credits.c3: No garden was harmed in the making of this game. Except one.
credits.c4: Thanks for reaching the bottom — and coming back.
credits.c5: The game isn't over. Keep digging. Just climb out in time.
credits.title: Credits
diary.title: Grandpa's diary
diary.sealed_depth: The page is sealed. Grandpa wrote on the strip: "Go deeper and you'll read it."
diary.sealed_event: The page is sealed. Grandpa wrote on the strip: "Do the job first. Then read."
diary.new_pages: A new page in Grandpa's diary. Visit the grave.
grave.tip_body: A slab, grass, a few flowers. Quiet.
grave.tip_diary_body: Read the pages. New ones open by themselves.
grave.epitaph: Here lies Grandpa. Next to the garden that did him in.
quest.grave: Task: visit Grandpa's grave — by the garden fence, right of the door
diary.first.text: Found a little stone. Yellow, heavy. Granny says it's rubbish. Granny can't tell gold from brass. The potatoes can wait.
diary.first.note: Iron and lead — for a pickaxe. Lead is heavy: don't get greedy.
diary.peat.text: The earth turned black, smells of hay. Granny says: fuel. I say: rubbish. Argued till night. She's right, the pest.
diary.peat.note: Peat burns — distil it into fuel. Selling it is a disgrace.
diary.diamond.text: Found a stone inside a stone: cobble on every side, as if on purpose. The pickaxe cracked. Beautiful, the swine. No regrets.
diary.diamond.note: A vein walled in by rock on all sides has something good inside. Don't spare the pickaxe — buy a new one.
diary.relic.text: Dug up not gold but a thing. Patterned, warm. It lay as if someone had put it there and waited. Put it — and never came back.
diary.relic.note: The older the thing, the deeper it lies. Take it to the museum, don't sell it.
diary.gold.text: The deeper, the yellower. My hands shake. Granny calls me to supper. Supper! With this going on!
diary.gold.note: Gold grows thicker with depth. Later it thins out — but never runs dry. Don't sit in one layer.
diary.heavy.text: My back won't bend. Gold is heavy, the pest. Threw out the lead — no regrets. That's how you learn to choose.
diary.heavy.note: You can't carry much on your back. Tossing good stuff to fit more in? Find a machine.
diary.whisper.text: I hear the earth. She quietly asks: a little more. And I dig. Since then I write down what she shows me: I could never dig this far myself.
diary.whisper.note: Deep down lie titanium, platinum, lithium — for machines. Coal is the step toward them.
diary.rig.text: Blueprint. A machine: drill in front, cab, wings. Digs sideways and down, flies by itself. I won't make it. You, whoever you are — make it. And look after Granny.
diary.rig.note: The machine needs coal. Later — uranium, but it costs: mercury and coin.
diary.gems.text: Red and green, right in the wall, like sweets. Weigh nothing, worth a house. A fool takes lead.
diary.gems.note: Ruby and emerald go in the backpack first. Leave the lead and peat.
diary.lava.text: The walls are hot. Below it's red, flowing. She whispers: don't be afraid. I am afraid. The one who isn't afraid stays there.
diary.lava.note: Don't dig long in the heat. What you find deeper can't be sold: keep it for armour.
diary.monsters.text: Something's stirring down there. I don't like it when things stir. Dress up if you go. The five things from the museum aren't a prize, they're clothes.
diary.monsters.note: Helmet, breastplate, shield, amulet, gauntlet — collect all five before going deeper.
diary.bottom.text: There's no bottom. There's a place where she has nothing left to ask for. It's quiet there. Terribly quiet.
diary.bottom.note: The gauntlet has five sockets — for the five deepest stones. Look for them at the very bottom.
diary.last.text: The grandson got out. On his own. All my life I called Grandpa an "old fool". Now I say "old fool, but ours". — Granny
